premise: Build Pellier’s governed agentic retail system, from grounded product discovery to verifiable customer actions.
throughline: Know the facts → respect the requirements → establish the caller → govern the action.

labs.name: Marco
labs.title: Build a PostgreSQL-Grounded Agent
labs.need: Marco needs reliable stock and dispatch facts before his trip.
labs.next: You can check a product. Next, help Anna find the right product without changing her requirements.
labs.summary: Connect the inventory tool, then check that the agent answers from its returned facts. Keep an unknown product distinct from a known product with zero stock.
labs.todo: Task 1A: implement the inventory result contract. Task 1B: wire the specialist and prove a real Storefront turn.
labs.b: Make the agent use the facts
labs.proof: Exact turn, tool result, warehouse rows; unknown is not zero.

labs.name: Anna
labs.title: Build and Measure PostgreSQL Hybrid Retrieval
labs.need: Anna needs a gift under $100. Alternatives may change her preferences, never her requirements.
labs.next: You can find suitable products. Next, deploy Theo’s support capability and preserve the caller’s identity across the tool boundary.
labs.summary: Explain how search results are ranked, then keep budget, stock and exclusions unchanged when the agent retries with a different preference.
labs.todo: Task 2A: reconstruct recorded RRF. Task 2B: preserve the original requirements in every fallback attempt.
labs.proof: RRF arithmetic, fallback contract, exact returned IDs and SQL eligibility.

labs.name: Theo
labs.title: Deploy and Operate Agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
labs.need: Theo wants remembered preferences and help with his own service history. Context must not become permission.
labs.next: You can read under the right identity. Next, follow Jessica’s action through authorization, database effects and staff review.
labs.summary: Connect a tool that reads the signed-in customer’s support records, deploy it, and test access to their own records and another customer’s records.
labs.todo: Task 3A: reconcile publication, tool access and caller binding. Task 3B: deploy, challenge scope and identify the build that answered.
labs.proof: Owned and foreign request results, fresh session, executed build; Memory is context.

labs.name: Jessica
labs.title: Build Governed Agent Actions with Cedar
labs.need: Jessica needs her service request resolved safely. Staff must establish what happened before choosing the next action.
labs.next: Bring the four claims together: facts, requirements, caller and effect. Save your evidence and the next production question.
labs.summary: Write ownership checks in Cedar and PostgreSQL, then follow Jessica’s staff proposal through human confirmation to one recorded return.
labs.todo: Task 4A: author Cedar and distinguish five outcomes. Task 4B: test RLS and keyed evidence, then reconcile a human-reviewed return.
labs.b: Test ownership and reconcile the case
labs.proof: Rollback-only RLS probes, keyed absence with a positive control, exact review-to-return lineage.
